ask: Users want Claude to explain its own current features and guide setup and troubleshooting while they work.
plugin: A version-aware skill backed by an official-docs MCP index answers questions in session and runs a project preflight command for applicable best practices.

ask: Plugin authors want correct installation, marketplace, source, version and distribution guidance.
plugin: A skill and validation command inspect plugin manifests, source layouts, marketplace entries, dependency state and release versions, then produce concrete fixes.

ask: Authors want reliable guidance for skill discovery, imports, frontmatter, nested definitions and reload behavior.
plugin: A skill plus a bin linter checks skill and agent trees, resolves precedence and namespace collisions, and explains reload and tool visibility in context.

ask: Hook authors want accurate event contracts, blocking semantics, output shapes and runnable examples.
plugin: A skill and bin validator inspect hook configuration and sample event payloads, simulate exit-code and output handling, and flag rules that cannot load.

ask: Users want to configure MCP servers and diagnose authentication, protocol, discovery and tool-list failures.
plugin: A command with an MCP diagnostics server inspects configured servers, tests stdio and HTTP handshakes, checks stdout framing and guides reconnect or retry.

ask: Users want the effective configuration, settings keys, source precedence and supported command syntax to be discoverable.
plugin: An MCP reference and diagnostic command read settings from their scopes, show the effective value and validate documented keys against the installed Claude Code version.

ask: Users want to understand model selection, fallback, context limits and agent model inheritance.
plugin: A skill and command inspect available models and current settings, explain effective routing and recommend a configured fallback chain for each surface.

ask: Users want predictable approval, deny and sandbox behavior before running sensitive operations.
plugin: A settings hook and audit command explain the effective permission rules for a proposed tool call and enforce project policy on paths and commands.

ask: Users want correct delegation, nested agents, team configuration and specialist tool access.
plugin: A skill and agent templates guide team and subagent setup, validate frontmatter and tools visibility, and suggest compatible dispatch patterns.

ask: Users want to inspect background agents and recover stalled or lost task output.
plugin: A statusline and command read agent and task state, surface blocked sessions and output paths, and guide safe stop or recovery.

ask: Users want reliable worktree isolation, configuration inheritance and cleanup.
plugin: A command and settings hook inspect the current worktree, shared git metadata and cleanup targets, warn on writes across boundaries, and guide safe removal.

ask: Users want to understand session storage, fork and resume behavior and recover conversation state.
plugin: A command indexes local session JSONL and saved outputs, offers recap and named resume targets, and documents what a fork or clear preserves.

ask: Developers want dependable print mode, SDK and CI scripts with clear parity limits.
plugin: A skill and bin wrapper validate `claude -p` flags, stream JSON and environment, diagnose hangs, and provide tested invocation templates.

ask: Users want to discover terminal commands, shortcuts and input behavior without leaving the session.
plugin: A context-aware command and skill provide an interactive shortcut and command reference for the active terminal and surface.

ask: Users want to find, resume and manage Remote Control sessions across terminal and mobile surfaces.
plugin: A command and statusline show the current session link and location, explain surface availability and guide reconnect and resume steps.

ask: Users want to know what usage data and session content is sent, retained or omitted by each setting.
plugin: A command inspects environment and telemetry configuration, samples locally visible event shapes, and explains privacy and experiment controls.

ask: Users want actionable diagnosis of installation, authentication and gateway setup.
plugin: A bin diagnostic checks installed version, provider environment and connection prerequisites and gives exact recovery guidance for common configuration faults.

ask: Users want to understand context consumption, prompt caching and compaction behavior before work fails.
plugin: A function hook observes session usage and compaction events, shows a budget forecast, and a skill explains context and cache tradeoffs.

ask: Users want better output styles and access to useful reasoning and response presentation controls.
plugin: An output style supplies a chosen writing format; an experimental function hook can expose permitted transcript metadata and render a custom view.

ask: Users want exact built-in tool names, behavior and capability limits for their current surface.
plugin: A version-aware MCP reference and skill map displayed labels to canonical tools and give actionable per-tool examples.

ask: Non-English users want usable Claude Code guidance in their own language.
plugin: An output style and translated reference skill provide localized in-session guidance and correct misleading translated examples.

ask: Users want multi-model pipelines that choose different models for exploration, implementation and review.
plugin: An experimental function hook routes turn and subagent requests by task phase, offers configured model choices and records the selected path.

ask: Users want to inspect thinking blocks that exist in local session transcripts.
plugin: An experimental function hook reads available transcript messages and renders permitted thinking blocks in a local view.

ask: Users want to type literal @path text without triggering Claude Code file import.
plugin: An experimental function hook rewrites prompt input before native path expansion according to a configurable escape rule.

ask: Desktop users want a visible fast-mode state and an easier way to toggle it.
plugin: An experimental function hook adds a small desktop UI indicator and toggle backed by the exposed configuration API.
